children: Gold was little changed on Monday as market participants awaited key U.S. inflation data due later this week for further clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate path.
FUNDAMENTALS
* Spot gold
was almost unchanged at $4,424.40 per ounce, as of 0025 GMT. U.S. gold futures
for December delivery were down 0.1% at $4,471.60.

* Data on Friday showed U.S. job growth accelerated sharply in August while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, suggesting an improvement in the labour market after recent struggles and keeping a rate increase this month on the table. Gold prices slipped after the data.
* Traders are pricing in a 58% chance of a rate hike at the Fed's September 15-16 meeting, CME's FedWatch tool showed.
* While gold is typically viewed as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to weigh on the appeal of non-yielding bullion.
* U.S. consumer and producer inflation reports are due this week.
* U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that unless the Fed cuts interest rates, he would stop trading with countries with which the United States had a deficit.

* Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said on Friday that weak productivity and shocks such as COVID-19 were behind a climb in public debt across advanced economies, which in turn was pushing up borrowing costs.
* Perth Mint's gold product sales in August hit a three-month low, while silver sales slipped more than 31% from a month earlier, the refiner said on Friday.
* Among other metals, spot silver
was flat at $66.21 per ounce, platinum
lost 0.7% at $1,807.38 and palladium
declined 0.4% to $1,393.00.
